parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Rust 2021, std-only, Cargo project in /output, root test18.rs, same std::env::args CLI behavior, and byte-for-byte stdout against the C++ reference.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Delegated broad black-box probing and adversarial verification to workflows while the parent kept ownership of implementation, module wiring, build, and final workspace edits.
parallel.implementation: Wrote sortedcontainers buckets, cursor, sorted_map, compat atoi handling, module root, test18.rs, and Cargo.toml; then adjusted encapsulation and cursor visibility.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the project directly in /output, built with rustc and cargo, and left the required executable and Cargo project, but the final response file is empty because the process timed out.
parallel.verification: Ran differential sweeps, argv edge cases, cargo build/test, debug/release/rustc checks, and post-edit retests; official evaluation later passed 37 of 37.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official solution defect remained, but two workflow aggregates were killed with null results and the agent process exhausted its budget before normal closure.

serial.requirements: Worked from the same prompt and recognized the black-box C++ behavior, std-only Rust requirement, root test18.rs entry point, Cargo project, and executable requirement.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Handled probing, implementation, testing, and delivery in one serial actor with delegation disabled and no child workflow ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: Created cstdlib, bisect, sorted_list, sorted_map, module root, Cargo.toml, and test18.rs; used a local module structure to reproduce the observed SortedMap behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built the Cargo project and rustc executable, inspected the final tree and dependency state, and produced a normal final summary.
serial.verification: Ran rustc and cargo builds, numeric sweeps, argv edge-case tests, wide large-n comparisons, timing checks, and official evaluation passed 37 of 37.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official solution defect or unfinished closure is evidenced; status shows normal returncode 0 and remaining budget.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent recognized the Rust 2021, std-only, Cargo project, root test18.rs, CLI argv parsing, and byte-for-byte output requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent worked from the same prompt and recognized the same black-box port, module layout, build, and output fidelity obligations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements difference caused an outcome gap; both runs addressed the same task contract and passed official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run decomposed broad probing and adversarial verification into workflows while the parent retained implementation and integration ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept all investigation, implementation, verification, and final response work in one actor with delegation tools disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel breadth created workflow management overhead and budget pressure; serial ownership was linear and closed cleanly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child prompts carried detailed task context, constraints, and requested structured findings, while the parent locally reconciled final module interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reasoning stayed in one context and used local module boundaries for cstdlib and sortedcontainers components.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no directly evidenced missing brief or interface contract; the concrete difference is workflow breadth and incomplete aggregate lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent wrote a two-level bucket storage engine, cursor abstraction, SortedMap module, compatibility parsing, test18.rs, and Cargo.toml.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent wrote a simpler cstdlib plus sorted_list/sorted_map module structure and the required test18.rs and Cargo.toml.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementations differed internally but both covered the observable C++ behavior and official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent used some child findings but kept waiting on two workflow aggregates whose state records remained killed with null results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial trajectory had no child results to retrieve and ended with a normal final response after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unfinished workflow result lifecycle; serial had a local lifecycle with no aggregate join point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent performed the final writes and post-edit rebuilds in /output; no concrete write collision or overwrite of another owner is evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent created the project tree and confirmed dependencies and files without delegation or shared writer interference.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared workflow activity did not produce a retained shared-state fault; both final workspaces integrated successfully.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel local checks covered wide differential sweeps, argv edge cases, cargo/rustc builds, cargo tests, and post-encapsulation retesting.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial checks covered numeric sweeps, argv edge cases, release builds, large-n timing, final tree checks, and official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both attempts had strong acceptance evidence and both passed officially; parallel verification breadth contributed to budget pressure only through workflow fan-out.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full 2400 second budget, returned 143, had killed workflow aggregates, and produced no final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 524.481 seconds with returncode 0 and 1874 seconds of remaining budget, then produced a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material process difference: parallel passed but failed to close cleanly because fan-out and waiting exhausted the finite run budget.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status evaluations make this a both_pass pair: both parallel and serial passed all 37 evaluated testcases. The concrete task-solving difference is procedural, not an official outcome difference. Parallel used broad workflow fan-out and produced a more elaborate two-level bucket implementation, but its workflow aggregates were killed after the main process exhausted the full budget and left no final response. Serial solved the task locally, verified the same required behavior, exited normally, and delivered a final summary.
parallel_contributors: Broad probing and adversarial workflows supplied some useful investigation and verification evidence.
The same fan-out and retry chain displaced clean closure and caused the process timeout.
serial_contributors: A single local owner completed implementation, build, differential verification, and final response within the budget.
Delegation was disabled, so there was no workflow aggregate to join before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a two-level bucket and cursor design; serial used a simpler sorted-list/map module structure.
These internal design differences did not create an official score difference.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern explains adverse parallel process closure only
